entities.summary:
Albert II, Duke of Austria, ruled as the Wise or the Lame from 1330 to 1358, playing a pivotal role in the Habsburg dynasty's expansion across Central Europe. As duke of Austria and Styria, he oversaw significant territorial gains and strengthened the power of the Habsburgs. This period of growth was marked by the Black Death, which significantly impacted the demographics and economy of the region.


 The consequences of Albert II's rule can be seen in the enduring legacy of the Habsburgs, who would go on to shape European politics and culture for centuries to come. His diplomatic efforts and strategic alliances with neighboring lords contributed to the stability of the region during a time of great upheaval.


 The impact of the Black Death on the demographics of Austria and Styria cannot be overstated, with estimates suggesting that up to 60% of the population was lost. This demographic shift had far-reaching consequences for the region's economy, politics, and culture.


 Albert II's legacy is also marked by his role in the development of the Austrian economy, which would go on to become a major player in European trade and commerce.
